### Network Setup

```{r}
# Load Network 
read <- read.csv("network_data.csv", 
                    sep = ";", 
                 # Skip rows in csv beginning with "#"
                    comment.char = "#", 
                    header = FALSE)

# Select relevant vars and tidy 
network <- read |> 
  # Add prefix to distinguish distinct nodes (bipartite)
  mutate(female_node = paste0("f_", V1), 
         male_node = paste0("m_", V2)) |> 
  select(female_node, male_node) |> 
  distinct() # Drop duplicate pairs

# Create the graph 
g <- graph_from_data_frame(network, directed = FALSE)
g <- simplify(g)

# Check if the network connected
is_connected(g) # FALSE
# Identify largest connected component (LCC)
components_g <- components(g)
# Create new graph extracting nodes in LCC
g <- induced_subgraph(g, which(components_g$membership == which.max(components_g$csize)))

# Assign node type as a vertex attribute
# Escorts = TRUE, Buyers = FALSE (as per igraph bipartite convention <-- CHECK THIS)
V(g)$type <- startsWith(V(g)$name, "f_")

# Check graph properties 
is_bipartite(g) # TRUE

# Check number of nodes and edges after extraction
vcount(g) # Number of nodes 
ecount(g) # Number of edges

# Other attributes
# Separate degree distributions
deg_escorts <- degree(g)[V(g)$type == TRUE]
deg_buyers  <- degree(g)[V(g)$type == FALSE]
data.frame(
  type = c("Escorts", "Buyers"),
  n = c(length(deg_escorts), length(deg_buyers)),
  mean = c(mean(deg_escorts), mean(deg_buyers)),
  median = c(median(deg_escorts), median(deg_buyers)),
  sd = c(sd(deg_escorts), sd(deg_buyers)))
```
